entries.title: Diagnosis: reoon verification call failed
entries.detail: Cause (most likely): the GitHub secret REOON_API_KEY was pasted with its .env comment; the failing URL carries the key followed by spaces and '# reoon.com email verifier: free daily credits', so Reoon rejects it with 401. The local .env loader strips ' #' comments, GitHub does not. The key was also written in plain text into this issue's detail and log J0139 on the data branch. Remedy: rotate the Reoon key, set the GitHub secret to the bare key only, and change HttpError/provider errors to redact key= and api_key= query values; then clean the stored issue/log text. entries.detail: Cause: inbox reads (IMAP) had no time limit, so a dropped connection hung the sender for hours. Fix: every IMAP connection now gives up after 60 s (tested against a silent server). Live since 16:36 on 23 Nov: PR 17 merged (7923bdb) and pulled into the Mac sender's folder. The 16:45 run finished in under a minute. A real Mac sleep during a read has not been seen yet.

entries.title: Solved: A concurrent sync can undo a send claim, so an email could go out twice
entries.detail: Cause: store.sync reset the data folder without holding the store lock, so another process could wipe a send claim (and once, a settle). Fix: sync now takes the lock (reproduced before, gone after). Live since 16:36 on 23 Nov: PR 17 merged (7923bdb) and pulled into the Mac sender's folder. Correction: the 22 Nov audit of stored records could not rule out a past double send. Checked again: no message ID was claimed twice in 310 claims on the data branch. That is strong evidence, not proof; Gmail Sent was not checked. Seen in effect on 23 Nov: M0409's sent mark and M0389's failure were lost while a scheduled agent wrote at the same time; the inbox check repaired both (M0409 found in Sent, M0389 not sent).
